record.original_question: Find a formula for the number of perfect matchings of the n-dimensional cube graph.

evidence.quote: One can also look at graphs that are bipartite but not planar. A natural example is the n-cube (that is, the n-dimensional cube with all sides of length 2).
Problem 19: Find a formula for the number of perfect matchings of the n-cube.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $Q_n$ denote the $n$-dimensional hypercube graph: its vertex set is $\{0,1\}^n$, and two vertices are adjacent if and only if they differ in exactly one coordinate. A perfect matching of $Q_n$ is a set $M$ of edges of $Q_n$ such that every vertex of $Q_n$ is incident to exactly one edge in $M$. Let $m(n)$ denote the number of perfect matchings of $Q_n$.

Find a closed-form formula (or explicit combinatorial/analytic expression) for $m(n)$ as a function of $n \ge 1$.
artifact.status_search_result: No closed-form formula for the number of perfect matchings of the n-cube is known. Exact values have been computed only for small n (through n = 7, giving 391,689,748,492,473,664,721,077,609,089 perfect matchings of Q_7), and asymptotic estimates exist, but a general formula remains elusive. Counting perfect matchings in bipartite graphs is #P-complete in general, suggesting fundamental difficulty.

status_evidence.title: Enumerating Perfect Matchings in n-Cubes
status_evidence.snippet: Dynamic programming approach used to compute the number of perfect matchings in the 7-cube.
status_evidence.claim: Exact values of pm(Q_n) known only up to n=7; no closed formula given.

status_evidence.title: A005271 - OEIS
status_evidence.snippet: Sequence of number of perfect matchings of n-cube; terms tabulated for small n.
status_evidence.claim: OEIS lists only finitely many computed values, with no general formula.
